8.3.2.4 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
Flow and channel characteristics indicate Bearcamp Creek to be of the small headwater pool and riffle type, surrounded by moderate to steep slopes that support moderate to dense vegetation, forming a symmetrical tight enclosure (Figure 8-4). No unique scenic or esthetic resources exist within the Bearcamp Creek alternative that cannot be found in the proposed Bad Creek site, as well as in the other alternative sites, and in many of the numerous adjacent valleys. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater esthetic attributes, the Bearcamp Creek site has been rated 7, compared with a rating of 3, 7, and 5 given to the proposed Bad Creek site, the Coley Creek site, and the Long Spur Ridge site, respectively (Dysart, et al., 1973).
Impacts on purely scenic and esthetic resources resulting from construction of this proposed alternative would drastically change the landscape, the degree of change depending on the size and character of the project lake and appurtenant facilities.
8.3.2.5 Recreation
This alternative would inundate considerably more combined land-water area providing recreational opportunities than the proposed Bad Creek Project. The site is located in one of the most remote and least developed areas of the region, adjacent to the Coley Creek site. Opportunities now exist for high-quality, low-density, primitive-type outdoor recreation in this area. Present accessibility to the site is poor, and no public use facilities exist. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater recreational attributes, the Bearcamp Creek site has been rated 8, compared with a rating of 4 for the Bad Creek site (Dysart, et al., 1973) The basis for the rating system is discussed in Subsection 8.3.1.5.
